name: Value chain
summary: Break the business into steps (e.g. R&D → sourcing → production → distribution → sales & marketing → service), then find where cost, value, margin or risk concentrates. Useful for cost, sustainability and integration questions.
opening_line: I'd walk the value chain from sourcing through production, distribution and sales, and see where the costs, the value and the problems concentrate.
when_to_use: Cost reduction: where is money spent?
Where to capture value in an industry
when_not_to_use: Pure demand-side questions like market sizing

buckets.name: Concentration
questions: Which step has the biggest cost, margin, emissions or risk?

industry_adaptations.note: Sourcing → DC → store → customer; shrink and last-mile costs.
Sustainability: raw-material sourcing is often the largest share of the emissions footprint.

common_mistakes: Listing steps without quantifying where the issue sits
